text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BERLINGSKE TIDENDE did not appear on Friday due to industrial action.
---Unibank is demanding compensation for losses it says it incurred as a result of insider trading at cleaninbg group ISS.
--- Denmark's tourist board is to expand its activities in France with the opening of a new office in Paris on March 10 this year.

---Pension giant ATP is to fire many of its brokers if they cannot improve their forecasts. Research shows that the brokers, representing the country's biggest houses, are only correct in their recommendations about 60 percent of the time.
--- Strikes and stoppages at Tele Danmark are likley to continue for several days, following the announcement of widespread staff cuts.

--- Denmark's largest convenience goods group FDB, selling 40 percent of all milk in Denmark, wants 25 percent of all FDB dairy products to be of its own brand instead of brands from dairies Kloever Maelk and MD Foods. FDB's own dairy brand could lower prices on dairy products.

--- Still more Danes are borrowing money from credit card companies instead of regular bank loans in spite of persistent advertising campaigns for cheap bank loans and warnings from the consumer council against expensive credit card loans.
--- A government study shows that proposed higher fuel taxes would bring billions of crowns in extra revenues despite reducing consumption.
